exposure: Mode of first delivery (normal vaginal, vaginal delivery complicated by instrumental intervention and/or obstetric anal sphincter injury, caesarean section)
vaginal deliveries complicated by instrumental intervention and/or obstetric anal sphincter injury (IVD ± OASIS)
outcome: Prevalence of anal incontinence (AI) from late pregnancy to 6 years postpartum
cohort: Women with their first deliveries between May 2009 and December 2010 in two Norwegian health regions (n=1571)
finding: While anal incontinence generally decreased from late pregnancy to one year postpartum, women with complicated vaginal deliveries had a higher prevalence of AI at six years postpartum compared to those with cesarean or normal vaginal deliveries, with age, bowel disease, and bowel evacuation problems also contributing to higher AI prevalence over time.
mod_finding: Women with complicated vaginal deliveries had a higher prevalence of anal incontinence at 6 years postpartum compared to those with cesarean or normal vaginal deliveries.
